title: Fennimore fraud-screening vendors
brief: Fennimore Payments processes about 6 million customer payment transactions a month and has to choose a fraud-screening vendor by 2026-11-20. The risk lead, Gideon Ashworth, wants a comparison page for the payments steering group. Three vendors. Tollgate: catches 91.2 percent of fraud, wrongly blocks 1.9 percent of good transactions, costs 4.10 dollars per 1000 transactions, integration takes 6 weeks. Vantage Shield: catches 94.8 percent, 3.1 percent wrongly blocked, 6.80 dollars per 1000, 10 weeks. Kestrel Risk: catches 89.5 percent, 1.2 percent wrongly blocked, 2.90 dollars per 1000, 4 weeks. At 6 million transactions a month the annual fees come to 295200 dollars for Tollgate, 489600 for Vantage Shield and 208800 for Kestrel Risk. Use the sections "Side by side", "Annual fees", "What the trade-off means" and "Recommendation". For the trade-off, explain that each wrongly blocked transaction is a customer declined at checkout, and that Vantage Shield's extra catch rate over Tollgate (3.6 points) comes with 1.2 points more wrongly blocked and 194400 dollars more in fees a year. We lean toward Tollgate as the balanced choice, with Kestrel Risk as the budget fallback if the steering group wants to cut fees by about 86400 dollars a year. State plainly that if the contract is signed by 2026-12-15, Tollgate and Kestrel Risk would be live before the change freeze on 2027-02-01 but Vantage Shield, at 10 weeks, would not.

edit.request: Kestrel Risk's price is now 3.40 dollars per 1000 transactions instead of 2.90, which makes its annual fees 244800 dollars.
